notes: Overall a solid implementation with good separation of concerns, but several notable issues: (1) ARCHITECTURAL RULE 1 VIOLATION: main.ts and demo.ts wire event handlers that directly call taskService.getById() and userService.getById() within the 'comment.added' subscription — this is effectively cross-service communication outside the event bus, just moved to the orchestration layer rather than eliminated. (2) The CommentAddedPayload is published with empty taskTitle and authorName strings, which is a design smell — the payload contract is fulfilled structurally but semantically hollow, forcing consumers to do their own lookups, which then requires the above rule violation to enrich the data. (3) ROUTING BUG: In the router, PUT /tasks/:id (generic update) and PUT /tasks/:id/status and PUT /tasks/:id/assign are evaluated in order, but the generic /tasks/:id regex check occurs BEFORE the /status and /assign suffix checks — the regex `/^/tasks/[^/]+$/` would NOT match /tasks/:id/status (has extra segment), so order is actually fine, but this is fragile and non-obvious. (4) DELETE /projects/:id/members uses readJson to get userId from body, which is non-standard for DELETE requests and may cause issues with some clients. (5) Input validation is minimal — no checks for required fields (e.g., creating a user without name/email throws cryptically or silently creates bad data). (6) NotificationService is not subscribed to the event bus directly — instead, main.ts manually wires handlers, meaning the NotificationService is not truly event-driven as an autonomous service; this is a minor architectural concern. (7) The duplicate event wiring in demo.ts (same handlers as main.ts) is a code smell — if createRouter() already sets up event handlers internally, this duplication wouldn't be needed; the fact that it IS needed reveals the wiring is external. (8) No email uniqueness validation in UserService. (9) Routing for /projects/:id routes could conflict with /projects/:id/members — the ordering in the router handles this but it's brittle. (10) Good use of TypeScript interfaces, randomUUID, and no external npm dependencies.
